The results revealed significant differences in student engagement and academic workload among the three phases. Middle school students had the highest scores of engagements, while high school suffered most academic workloads. These findings are expected to extend our understanding of K-12 online education in the context of China.

articleTitle: Introducing a Discussion Support System using Individual Audio Instruction to Activate Passive Members
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology & Education (TALE)
abstract: This paper proposes a system that supports a member whose utterance ratio in a group is smaller than other members. In this study, we targeted learning activities via face-to-face discussion in a small group. The ratios of utterance are often biased to particular members in such discussions; however, it is desirable for all members of a discussion to speak actively. To solve this problem, the proposed system provides different messages based on the utterance ratio of each member. These messages are formed to encourage passive members and are delivered to each member individually using earphones. This allows us to provide different instructions to all members of the group. The proposed system was employed in experimental discussions to evaluate the effectiveness of the individual audio instructions. The experimental results demonstrate that the ratios of utterances of the target members were improved temporarily by the individual audio instructions. However, some of the members were unaffected by the individual audio instructions and a post-discussion questionnaire revealed that such members viewed several features of the proposed system unfavorably.

articleTitle: An Overview of China-New Zealand Joint Cooperative Higher Education Programs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology & Education (TALE)
abstract: As a rapidly expanding economy with a growing population, China has been looking to foreign countries and institutions to assist in developing capacity in its education system. New Zealand has been helping to develop the human resources of China for many years mainly through enrolling students in its higher educational institutions. Of late, New Zealand has also been supporting the development of China's education capacity by working with Chinese institutions in establishing and delivering formally approved Sino-Foreign joint educational programs in China. Based on our research and to the best of our knowledge, as of August 2021, there are 35 active China-New Zealand joint programs at the Bachelor's degree level and above (i.e. at New Zealand Qualification Framework Level 7 and above). It involves 14 New Zealand providers (i.e. 6 universities, 7 institutes of technology or polytechnics and 1 private institution) and 27 Chinese institutions across 14 provinces in China. These 35 joint programs have provided tertiary education opportunities for almost 13,300 Chinese students annually, based on their approved intake quotas.

articleTitle: Communication Network Experiment Design Based on Virtual Simulation Platform
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology & Education (TALE)
abstract: Modern communication technology is bringing new development opportunities for many fields with strong network capabilities, and there is an urgent demand for communication professionals. Practical teaching is an important method for cultivating innovative talents for engineering majors. Based on the virtual simulation platform, this paper designs some wireless communication network experiments, including network architecture experiments: wireless access network, core network and bearer network deployment; wireless communication network key technologies experiments: network slicing, wireless resource management and beam management. Each experiment is designed with experimental content, experimental requirements, capability requirements and personalized requirements. The experimental results demonstrate that the designed experiments are helpful to the cultivation of students' innovative ability while testing the theory.

articleTitle: Educational Robot Aided Photo Taking and Management
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology & Education (TALE)
abstract: Photo taking and management can make trouble or waste time sometimes. Therefore, this paper develops the educational robot service to provide better photography and management services. People are enthusiasm in photo taking, but they don't have enough time to manage their own photos, because manually selecting and managing personal photos is very laborious and time consuming. In view of these difficulties in taking photos, as well as the low efficiency of users' storage and management of photos in the context of massive photos, this paper adopts artificial intelligence technology to overcome the deficiencies of existing camerawork activities. This paper uses intelligent technology to equip educational robots to provide services. These services can assist in taking photos and post-photo management. In the scenario of photo taking, it helps people to take good photos. During the photo management phase, it uses cloud technology to deliver and process photos. This service saves people's precious time and enhances a better photography experience.

articleTitle: IEEETALE 2021
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology & Education (TALE)
abstract: TALE, an international conference on engineering, technology, and education is the IEEE Education Society's premier conference series in the Asia-Pacific region. It aims to provide a forum for scholars and practitioners to share their knowledge and experience in engineering and technology education, as well as in technology-enabled educational innovation across a variety of academic and professional disciplines. The target audience of the conference is diverse and includes those working in the higher education, vocational education and training (VET), K-12, corporate, government and healthcare sectors.

articleTitle: Welcome to the Microworld: STEAM Education Approach to Learn Plant Ultrastructure Cell Biology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology & Education (TALE)
abstract: Currently, the gamut of teaching tools and materials has been dramatically widened through state-of-the-art technologies. It has been proposed that these techniques could be exploited in STEAM education to improve pedagogical efficacy, foster scientific thinking, and raise appreciation of science via multisensory creativity in diverse settings. Here, this work-in-progress paper illustrated to model 3D-printed organelles with complex membrane structures using raw experimental data and remodel plastids using beeswax as STEAM education to foster learner's creativity. As a stratagem in STEAM education, a combination of 3D modeling with hands-on creative activity was proven to be efficacious for K-12 learners.
